2608.07169.title: Agent Memory Distillation: Empowering Small LLM Agents with Hierarchical Teacher Memory
2608.07169.paper_summary: Memory systems have shown promise for improving agent performance, but their potential remains largely unexplored for small language models, which struggle to generate sufficient successful trajectories on their own. We propose Agent Memory Distillation (AMD), a training-free framework that transfers structured knowledge from a large teacher agent to a small student agent through hierarchical memory. AMD constructs three complementary memory types from successful teacher trajectories: Workflow memory encodes task-level strategies, Subtask memory provides concrete behavioral examples at an intermediate granularity, and Function memory captures per-function calling conventions and common pitfalls. Workflow and Subtask memories are injected proactively at the start of each task, while Function memory is retrieved reactively upon tool-calling errors. We evaluate AMD on three tool-use benchmarks using four student models (4B-8B parameters) with GPT-5-mini as the teacher, achieving average accuracy gains of 27.2%p, 11.2%p, and 3.4%p on AppWorld, BFCL V3, and ToolSandbox, while consistently outperforming existing memory-based baselines. Further analysis shows that Subtask memory contributes the largest gains, teacher effectiveness depends on both teacher capability and student compatibility, and 4B-sized students benefit most from AMD.
2608.07169.paper_summary_zh: 記憶系統在提升代理性能方面顯示出潛力，但對於小型語言模型而言，其潛力仍然大多未被探索，這些模型在獨立生成足夠成功的軌跡方面存在困難。我們提出了代理記憶蒸餾（Agent Memory Distillation，AMD），這是一個無需訓練的框架，通過層級記憶將結構化知識從大型教師代理轉移到小型學生代理。AMD 從成功的教師軌跡構建三種互補的記憶類型：工作流程記憶編碼任務級策略，子任務記憶提供中等粒度的具體行為示例，而函數記憶捕捉每個函數的調用約定和常見陷阱。工作流程和子任務記憶在每個任務開始時主動注入，而函數記憶則在工具調用錯誤時被反應性檢索。我們在三個工具使用基準上評估了 AMD，使用四個學生模型（4B-8B 參數），以 GPT-5-mini 作為教師，在 AppWorld、BFCL V3 和 ToolSandbox 上實現了平均準確率增益分別為 27.2%p、11.2%p 和 3.4%p，同時持續超越現有的基於記憶的基準。進一步分析顯示，子任務記憶貢獻了最大的增益，教師的有效性取決於教師能力和學生兼容性，而 4B 大小的學生從 AMD 中受益最多。
